severity_name: HEAVY SLOP WARNING — TRAVEL INTEGRITY ADVISORY
headline: HEAVY SLOP WARNING: PHANTOM-ITINERARY FRONT SWEEPS INTO TRAVEL REGIONS AS AI-GENERATED DESTINATION GUIDES SEND REAL TOURISTS TO SCENIC OVERLOOKS, CHARMING CAFES, AND 'HIDDEN GEM' WATERFALLS THAT HAVE NEVER EXISTED AT ANY COORDINATE ON EARTH
advisory: A deep synthetic low has settled over the travel-planning corridor, producing confident, beautifully formatted itineraries for places that are not there. The Service advises residents to independently verify that a recommended landmark exists before driving four hours toward it. Where a guide describes a 'quaint family-run bakery beloved by locals since 1923,' residents should confirm the presence of both the bakery and the locals. Ground truth remains the only reliable forecasting instrument.

regional_outlook.conditions: Dense itinerary fog with embedded phantom addresses. Top-ranked 'Ultimate 7-Day Guide' results confidently route travelers through at least two towns that have no legal existence.
A newly surveyed region, already eroded. Expect walls of stock-sunset prose and 'off-the-beaten-path' tips that are off the beaten path because no path was ever beaten there.
Scattered 'Your Personalized Trip Plan' emails arriving with high confidence and low correspondence to reality. Each contains one real restaurant surrounded by four generated ones.
Trip-planner apps multiplying along the lowlands, each promising AI itineraries. Reviews warm, destinations imaginary, refund buttons purely decorative.
Aesthetic hazard advisory. Pinnable 'dream getaway' boards depict turquoise coves rendered by a model that has never been to a coast, nor consulted a tide table.

specimen.status: Abundant and migratory; follows the scent of trending travel keywords.
specimen.habitat: Nests in destination guides, 'hidden gems' listicles, and the confident middle paragraph of any article titled 'You Won't Believe This Underrated Town.'
specimen.field_marks: Recognizable by its suspiciously perfect name (the 'Whispering Pines Overlook'), its lack of a verifiable address, and its endorsement by 'locals' who are never quoted, photographed, or geographically located.
specimen.call: Just a 15-minute drive from the town center, this breathtaking hidden gem offers stunning panoramic views that most tourists completely miss — be sure to arrive early to beat the crowds.
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for a genuine small-town attraction, which it is impersonating. Distinguish them by attempting to navigate there: a real landmark has a pin, a parking lot, and a gift shop; the Phantom Landmark has a five-star aggregate rating and no coordinates. If the map app spins and apologizes, you have found one.

spotter_tip: Before trusting any 'hidden gem,' search its exact name plus the word 'reviews.' If the only pages describing it are other guides describing it in the same three adjectives, you are not looking at a destination — you are looking at an echo.
tomorrow: Phantom itineraries persist through midday before a drizzle of fabricated 'local festivals' moves into the events regions; pack skepticism and a paper map.
